_sources_comment: WARROOM-FRESHNESS-001 Phase 1 — per-source registry, built from WARROOM_TILE_INVENTORY.md (173 rows), cross-referenced against docs/RUN_LOG_COVERAGE.md and sasmaster.ops.run_log. expected_cadence_seconds is populated ONLY where a real producing cron/LaunchAgent exists and its schedule is confirmed live. generate-status-js.human_name: War Room page generator (the snapshot writer itself)
generate-status-js.producer: cron */5 * * * * (RUN_LOG_COVERAGE row 21, wired=proposed-no — NOT wired to run_log)
dependent_tiles: the majority of STALE-classified tiles across OPS, AGENTS, QUEUE, TELEMETRY, CANVAS, cross-tab — see WARROOM_TILE_INVENTORY.md, any row whose Blocking-gap cites 'generate-status.js itself is not wired to run_log'
generate-status-js.note: This is the single biggest freshness gap on the whole board: the generator's own cron fires every 5 min but writes no run_log row, so every tile it feeds is honestly STALE (not LIVE) under this document's rule regardless of how fresh the underlying data actually is. Wiring generate-status.js to run_log (a small, well-scoped fix — RUNLOG-001 explicitly skipped rewriting its 'cd && node' chain shape rather than guess at a safe rewrite) would upgrade dozens of tiles from STALE to LIVE-capable in one move. Flagged as a high-leverage follow-up, not built here.

hardcoded-static-arrays.note: These are not 'sources with an unknown cadence' — they are hardcoded literals with NO backing source at all. Assigning them a cadence would be meaningless; the fix is deleting the hardcoding (a render-code change, out of this card's registry-only Phase 1 scope), not registering a cadence for fabricated data. Excluded from the Phase 2 decision-gate table for this reason — flagging the distinction explicitly so a future pass doesn't try to rule a cadence for a MOCK tile.
